# Discussion {#sec-discussion}

## Main findings

Twelve weeks of supervised training improved cardiorespiratory fitness by an
amount that exceeds the smallest difference generally considered clinically
relevant.

## Comparison with previous work

The magnitude of the effect is consistent with earlier trials in younger
populations [@garber2011], suggesting that trainability is preserved into the
eighth decade.

## Strengths and limitations

Supervision meant the delivered dose was known, which is unusual in this
literature. The trial was, however, single-centre and not blinded to
participants.

## Conclusion

A supervised 12-week programme produced clinically relevant improvements in
cardiorespiratory fitness in community-dwelling older adults.
